theorem prop_13_1_2 {u v : Ω → ℝ} (hu : Integrable u μ) (huv : Integrable (fun ω => u ω * v ω) μ)
    (hu0 : ∀ ω, 0 ≤ u ω) {M : ℕ → Set Ω} (hM : ∀ n, MeasurableSet (M n)) (hmono : Monotone M)
    {g H : ℕ → ℝ} {r₀ r₁ : ℕ} (h01 : r₀ ≤ r₁)
    (hg : ∀ n, r₀ ≤ n → n < r₁ → g (n + 1) ≤ g n) (hg0 : 0 ≤ g r₁)
    (hv : ∀ n, r₀ ≤ n → n ≤ r₁ → ∀ ω ∉ M n, v ω ≤ g n)
    (hH : ∀ n, r₀ ≤ n → n < r₁ → ∫ ω in M (n + 1), u ω ∂μ ≤ H n) (hH₁ : ∫ ω, u ω ∂μ ≤ H r₁) :
    ∫ ω in (M r₀)ᶜ, u ω * v ω ∂μ ≤
      g r₀ * (H r₀ - ∫ ω in M r₀, u ω ∂μ) + ∑ n ∈ Ioc r₀ r₁, g n * (H n - H (n - 1)) :=

note: Lean's discrete form implies (13.6) for integer r₁ under the book's monotonicity; it drops δ₀ ≤ x/2r₁² and needs only nested arcs. The book's proof needs r₁ ∈ ℤ, which its statement omits; Lean takes integer r₁. minor_arcs_input (Helfgott.Inputs) cites it only as the downstream application.
